target_customer: Companies and teams (HR and team leads) that want to measure and improve employee wellbeing
problem: Teams struggle with burnout and poor wellbeing but generic perks do not identify the underlying causes for a given team.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for teams and organizations
product_category: Employee wellbeing and team performance assessment platform

founders.name: Arosha Brouwer
founders.background_notes: Former strategy consultant and industry executive with about 15 years in digitization and team performance, per YC page.

founders.name: Lucy Howie
previous_startups: Tech startup in the innovation space (successful exit, name not stated on YC page)
founders.background_notes: Later an executive at a German unicorn building algorithmic products, per YC page.

exit.reason: Dutch HR tech company TrueTribe acquired Quan and integrated it into its wellbeing portfolio; terms undisclosed.

technical_complexity.rationale: A survey and matching platform is standard web software; the difficulty lay in a validated wellbeing instrument, later published as the Quan Well-being Index.

defensibility.rationale: A validated assessment and aggregated team data give some edge, but the wellbeing software market had many vendors and low switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large wellbeing vendors did not copy it; a small Dutch HR tech firm absorbed it in 2025.

market_need_then: Post pandemic burnout and remote work drove employer interest in wellbeing in 2021 and 2022, and TechCrunch framed the raise around that burnout wave.

branding.domain_note: Used quanwellbeing.com with a descriptive suffix; the site later redirected to TrueTribe.

brand_strength.rationale: Regional Dutch startup press and a YC logo, but no sign of brand pull; the word Quan is also a common given name, which hurts search distinctiveness.

outcome_analysis: Quan raised a $1.15M pre-seed through YC in January 2022, then relied on a bridge round in April 2024 led by HearstLab and 4impact. Without a clearly larger round and in a crowded wellbeing market, it was acquired by TrueTribe in July 2025, which suggests a modest outcome rather than a breakout.
notes: Later seed figures (2.82M in Jan 2024, 4.0M total) appear only on aggregators and conflict, so they are not recorded as rounds. A Masawa investment was mentioned without a date or amount. Silicon Canals reported the pre-seed as 1.03M euros. No competitor source dated near Jan 2022 was found, only current aggregator listings. The acquirer name and July 2025 date come from a search result summary of the Hague Business Agency page, not independently cross-checked.
